findings.reason: Untrusted source: hostif = interface->cur_altsetting captured at gigaset_probe entry (line 654); its endpoint[] flex-array length is solely the descriptor-declared bNumEndpoints of the altsetting presented by a physically attacker-controlled USB gadget at enumeration, and drivers/usb/core/config.c (lines ~483-500, read in this snapshot) only allocates the array when num_ep > 0, so an altsetting with bNumEndpoints == 0 leaves hostif->endpoint NULL and 0/1-endpoint altsettings leave indices 0 and 1 partially or wholly out of bounds. Missing guarantee: gigaset_probe fetches &hostif->endpoint[0].desc at line 708 and &hostif->endpoint[1].desc at line 727 with no bNumEndpoints >= 2 check anywhere in usb-gigaset.c (grep of the whole file returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences); the only validation before these reads is interface number == 0, altsetting number == 0 and bInterfaceClass == 255 checks (lines 670-686), none of which constrains the endpoint count. Unsafe use: the OOB-reachable endpoint[0].desc.wMaxPacketSize becomes buffer_size that sizes ucs->bulk_out_buffer via kmalloc (lines 709-714) and usb_endpoint_num/usb_endpoint_maxp feed the bulk-out pipe state; endpoint[1].desc.wMaxPacketSize (line 738) sizes ucs->rcvbuf via kmalloc (lines 738-744), and endpoint->desc.bEndpointAddress/bInterval are then used to program usb_fill_int_urb for ucs->read_urb which is usb_submit_urb'd at line 757 (lines 746-750: usb_fill_int_urb(..., usb_rcvintpipe(udev, usb_endpoint_num(endpoint)), ucs->rcvbuf, buffer_size, gigaset_read_int_callback, cs, endpoint->bInterval)). A malicious gadget spoofing the M105 vendor/product ID (checked at lines 665-669: USB_M105_VENDOR_ID/PRODUCT_ID) with a class-255 interface-0 altsetting-0 declaring 0 or 1 endpoints gives a NULL-deref (endpoint == NULL) or out-of-bounds descriptor read at device plug-in, with the leaked wMaxPacketSize sizing kernel receive buffers and the leaked bEndpointAddress/bInterval programming a live interrupt URB - the same untrusted-descriptor-count vs assumed-index invariant as the seed cx231xx bug. Counterevidence checked: no bNumEndpoints reference anywhere in usb-gigaset.c; the sibling bas-gigaset.c has the identical unguarded pattern (endpoint[0] at line 2365, no bNumEndpoints in file) and st5481_usb.c demonstrates the correct in-tree fix pattern for this same subsystem (bNumEndpoints != 7 reject at st5481_usb.c:264-266).

Untrusted source: iface_desc = &interface->altsetting[0] captured at sur40_probe line 520; its endpoint[] flex-array is sized solely by the descriptor-declared bNumEndpoints of altsetting 0, which a physically attacker-controlled USB gadget controls at enumeration (config.c allocates the array only when num_ep > 0). Missing guarantee: sur40_probe indexes endpoint[4] with a fixed literal 4 (line 531) after checking only bInterfaceClass == 0xFF (lines 522-523); grep of the whole file returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences, so nothing validates that the altsetting declares at least 5 endpoints. Unsafe use: the endpoint is dereferenced immediately - endpoint->bEndpointAddress is compared at line 532 (if (endpoint->bEndpointAddress != TOUCH_ENDPOINT) return -ENODEV;) and then sur40->bulk_in_size = usb_endpoint_maxp(endpoint) and sur40->bulk_in_epaddr = endpoint->bEndpointAddress (lines 570-571) program the polled-input read path whose URB uses usb_rcvbulkpipe(sur40->usbdev, sur40->bulk_in_epaddr) (line 342), and the maxp value sizes sur40->bulk_in_buffer = kmalloc(sur40->bulk_in_size) (lines 572-573). A gadget spoofing the Samsung SUR40 vendor/product ID with a class-0xFF interface whose altsetting 0 declares fewer than 5 endpoints makes endpoint[4] an out-of-bounds read past the flex array (or NULL + 4*sizeof(endpoint) offset past a NULL array when bNumEndpoints == 0) at device plug-in; the leaked bEndpointAddress then only fails the TOUCH_ENDPOINT comparison in the typical case, but the usb_endpoint_maxp-derived buffer is allocated from the same unvalidated fetch on the pass-through path. Impact is OOB read at probe (crash class, same consequence family as the seed); the value check bounds but does not remove the OOB read itself. Counterevidence checked: no bNumEndpoints anywhere in sur40.c; trigger requires spoofing the SUR40 device ID, trivial for a physical gadget.

Untrusted source: the endpoint[] flex-array of interface 0 altsetting 0 is descriptor data supplied at enumeration by a physically attacker-controlled USB device; uea_bind (line 2529) only checks ifnum == UEA_INTR_IFACE_NO (0) and claims interfaces via claim_interface/usb_ifnum_to_if, never the endpoint count of interface 0. Missing guarantee: grep over the whole file shows bNumEndpoints occurs 0 times in ueagle-atm.c, so no code path validates that interface 0's altsetting[0] declares at least 1 endpoint. Unsafe use: uea_boot (line 2170, called from uea_bind line 2600 during usbatm_usb_probe) reads actconfig->interface[0]->altsetting[0].endpoint[0].desc.bInterval inline in the usb_fill_int_urb argument list (lines 2206-2210) and the URB is immediately usb_submit_urb'd (line 2212); a malicious gadget matching the Eagle/ADI ADSL modem device table with bNumEndpoints == 0 on interface 0 makes endpoint[0] a read past a never-allocated (NULL) endpoint array - a NULL-derived wild pointer dereference at device plug-in - or past a short array, and the garbage bInterval value is installed as the live interrupt URB's polling interval. This resolves the exact site fact f002 flagged unresolved at s01:drivers/usb/atm/ueagle-atm.c:2209 for this snapshot; the interface[0]/altsetting[0] levels are structurally in-bounds (bound interface of an accepted configuration) but the endpoint[0] level is unvalidated, which is this branch's invariant. Counterevidence checked: no bNumEndpoints reference anywhere in ueagle-atm.c; the usbatm core (drivers/usb/atm/usbatm.c) programs its rx/tx pipes from driver-supplied constant endpoint numbers, not from interface-0 descriptor arrays, and validates maxpacket != 0 only for its own channel endpoints, so no core-side check covers this read.

Untrusted source: iface_desc = interface->cur_altsetting captured at usb_pcwd_probe line 624; the endpoint[] array length is the device-declared bNumEndpoints at enumeration (config.c allocates it only when num_ep > 0, leaving it NULL for a 0-endpoint altsetting). Missing guarantee: usb_pcwd_probe checks only bInterfaceClass == USB_CLASS_HID (lines 626-630) before taking &iface_desc->endpoint[0].desc at line 634; grep of pcwd_usb.c returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences, so nothing validates that the HID-class interface declares at least 1 endpoint - a legal USB HID interface altsetting may declare bNumEndpoints == 0 (e.g. a vendor-defined HID gadget), making endpoint[0] a read past a NULL array. Unsafe use: endpoint->bEndpointAddress programs pipe = usb_rcvintpipe(udev, endpoint->bEndpointAddress) (line 644), endpoint->wMaxPacketSize sets usb_pcwd->intr_size (lines 657-658: intr_size = (le16_to_cpu(endpoint->wMaxPacketSize) > 8 ? ... : 8)) which sizes usb_pcwd->intr_buffer = usb_alloc_coherent(udev, usb_pcwd->intr_size, ...) (line 660), and the descriptor feeds the interrupt URB submitted at probe. Note the usb_endpoint_is_int_in(endpoint) check at line 637 happens on the already-fetched (possibly OOB) descriptor, i.e. after the unvalidated index dereference, so it does not prevent the OOB read; it does gate the pipe use on the leaked bytes looking like an interrupt-IN endpoint. Downgraded to medium because the type check usually rejects garbage before the pipe is armed, but the out-of-bounds descriptor read itself occurs unconditionally at plug-in for a 0-endpoint HID-class gadget matching the Berkshire USB product ID.

Untrusted source: hwarc_neep_init reads iface->cur_altsetting->endpoint[0].desc where iface is the probed UWB radio-control interface; the endpoint array length is the device-declared bNumEndpoints and config.c leaves it NULL when the altsetting declares 0 endpoints. Missing guarantee: grep of hwa-rc.c returns zero bNumEndpoints occurrences, and hwarc_probe performs no endpoint-count validation before hwarc_neep_init runs (neep init is called during probe/start of the HWA radio controller). Unsafe use: epd->bEndpointAddress and epd->bInterval are used directly in usb_fill_int_urb(usb_rcvintpipe(usb_dev, epd->bEndpointAddress), ..., epd->bInterval) at lines 706-710 and the URB is submitted with GFP_ATOMIC immediately (line 711) - a 0-endpoint altsetting makes &endpoint[0] a NULL-derived wild pointer dereference at probe, and a short array gives an OOB-read bInterval installed as the notification URB's polling interval. The same copied pattern exists in drivers/uwb/i1480/dfu/usb.c lines 245 and 302 (epd = &i1480_usb->usb_iface->cur_altsetting->endpoint[0].desc, zero bNumEndpoints in that file) and drivers/usb/wusbcore/wa-nep.c line 272 (endpoint[0] with no local check, though its caller wa_create validates bNumEndpoints < 3 for the same interface at wa-hc.c:42 before wa_nep_create, making the wusbcore site guarded by a sibling check on the same altsetting). Reported for hwa-rc.c as the cleanest instance; i1480 remains listed as a candidate because its probe-path ordering (whether firmware-start paths guarantee an endpoint) was not fully deep-read within this pass.

No compilation, Kconfig check, or USB-gadget reproducer was run (snapshot is read-only; builds would go under $TMPDIR): all findings are static source hypotheses with grep-level counterevidence (zero bNumEndpoints occurrences in the reported files), matching the seed mechanism class.

The sweep bounded candidates to literal endpoint[N] and endpoint + N patterns and files carrying usb_host_endpoint pointers; endpoint discovery via indirect pointer arithmetic or cached pointers was not exhaustively enumerated, and drivers/media/usb, drivers/net, and drivers/usb/core were excluded per the branch split.

For 0-endpoint altsettings the endpoint array is never allocated (config.c num_ep > 0 gate, read in this snapshot), so the exact fault for the reported sites is a NULL-array index (wild pointer) versus heap-adjacent OOB read for short arrays; the direction of the violated invariant is certain, the exact fault mode is not.
